ANAMORPHIC DESQUEEZER · IPHONE · IPAD · MAC

Anamorphic Desqueezer — batch geometry on Apple devices

Use Anamorphic Desqueezer on iPhone, iPad, or MacBook when you need a native flagship pipeline: import squeezed clips from FilmStudio or cinema cameras, dial 1.25× through 2× squeeze, preview in real time, and export clean widescreen masters without round-tripping through a full NLE for every pass.

iPhone / iPad on set: queue dailies on the cart, sanity-check lens orientation, and hand off ProRes or HEVC that already matches the village monitor. MacBook: same ratios and batch muscle for location pulls when you want keyboard shortcuts and larger scopes before you commit to Resolve or Avid. No app installed yet? Preview in Web Studio ↗.

For the long-form walkthrough (shoot → export, factors, mistakes), jump to Anamorphic geometry — detailed ↓.

CINELUT LIVE GRADE · MAC

CineLut Live Grade — live LUT & CDL on set

Use CineLut Live Grade when you want a camera feed over SDI or HDMI on a MacBook, with LUTs, ASC-CDL-style primaries, and scopes updating in real time while you record graded ProRes to disk—so dailies match what the DP signed off on.

Typical flow: connect a supported capture device → choose your input format and monitoring (waveform, parade, vectorscope) → load a show LUT and trim CDL until the look locks → record takes with timecode / burn-in options if you need them → export CDL, LUT, AMF, or EDL+CDL packages so Silverstack, DaVinci Resolve, or editorial can inherit the same grade without round-tripping guesses.

Why it saves money: you can lean on fast Mac storage and CPUs instead of expensive in-camera media for every roll, while still keeping a disciplined on-set signal path.

Wireless camera workflow support

CineLut Live Grade supports wireless camera monitoring workflows using HDMI/SDI wireless transmitters and macOS-compatible capture devices.

Connect your camera to a wireless video transmitter, send the signal to a receiver, connect the receiver to your Mac through an HDMI/SDI capture device, and use CineLut Live Grade for live LUT preview, CDL-style color adjustment, scopes, and recording.

WORKFLOW

Camera → Wireless Transmitter → Receiver → Capture Card → MacBook → CineLut Live Grade

Compatible workflow for cameras such as:

ARRI, RED, Blackmagic, Sony, Canon, Panasonic GH/GH4/GH5/GH6, Lumix S-series, Nikon, Fujifilm, and other HDMI/SDI cameras.

Note: Direct camera Wi‑Fi support depends on the camera model. For professional low-latency monitoring, CineLut Live Grade works best through HDMI/SDI wireless receiver and capture-card workflows.

Note: Wireless workflow latency typically ranges from approximately 0.06s to 0.5s depending on the transmitter, receiver, capture card, camera output, and network conditions. For the lowest-latency professional monitoring, use dedicated HDMI/SDI wireless systems and a low-latency capture device.

FILMSTUDIO · IPHONE · IPAD · MAC

FilmStudio — field-ready cinema camera on Apple devices

FilmStudio is for capture discipline: manual ISO, shutter, focus, and white balance; zebras, peaking, histogram and waveform; timecode and take naming; and export paths that match how video village labels reels. It pairs naturally with anamorphic rigs when you need honest framing before you de-squeeze in post.

On-set habit: build presets per lens serial, lock AE/AF when the block is stable, and tag takes while the slate is fresh so editorial and Anamorphic Desqueezer metadata stay aligned. On Mac (Apple Silicon), use the same App Store listing where Apple surfaces the Mac build.

After the shoot: move squeezed clips into Anamorphic Desqueezer or the Web Studio for ratio correction, or into CineLut Live Grade if you are live-grading from a camera feed on Mac.

WINDOWS

PC dailies — live anamorphic, grading, and post desqueeze

AnamorphicDesqueezePro on the Microsoft Store covers the full Windows pipeline—from live anamorphic preview and live grading on set through post desqueeze when you are ready to deliver.

  • Live anamorphic, live grading, and post desqueeze
  • Folder-based batch processing
  • CinemaScope presets from 2.39:1 through 2.76:1
  • 3D LUT + CDL grading for batch and monitoring
  • EDL + CDL export packages for Resolve and editorial conform
  • Local processing for longer clips and higher bitrates

Use CDL trims to lock a show LUT across a reel, then lean on EDL when editorial needs shot lists, handles, and reconform metadata alongside the corrected masters—the same handoff philosophy as CineLut Live Grade on Mac, tuned for Windows batch pipelines. Confirm squeeze and framing in the browser first with Web Studio ↗.

Microsoft Store — AnamorphicDesqueezePro Web Studio

Check in app: Store builds move often—open AnamorphicDesqueezePro and review the Microsoft Store listing and in-app export / grade panels for the exact EDL, CDL, and LUT options in your installed version before you freeze a deliverables memo.

DocRev Manager (Windows) — manage your film documents in one system: PDF, Word, call sheets, delivery memos, and revision notes without losing versions across the production.

  • PDF and Word production files in a searchable project library
  • Versioned records for call sheets, notes, and delivery paperwork
  • Fast lookup on set and in post when producers ask for the latest doc

Add CineSnap AI (Windows) when you need individual photo editing—full-frame looks, crops, and compare—then export in batch across a folder or gallery so weddings, stills pulls, and social crops ship with the same grade.

WHAT DESQUEEZE DOES

Squeezed frame → corrected frame → cinematic output.

Squeezed

Tall / incorrect preview

Desqueezed

Corrected wide frame

Final Output

Letterbox delivery

CHOOSE THE RIGHT FACTOR

Choose the right squeeze factor.

1.25× / 1.30×

Subtle mobile adapters and light squeeze looks.

1.33×

Common mobile anamorphic lenses (fast, reliable framing).

1.50× / 1.55×

Balanced cinematic look and wider corrected frame.

1.80×

Wider stylized look — preview carefully before export.

2.00×

Classic cinema anamorphic workflows and strong squeeze.

Quick check: If faces look too wide, the factor is too high. If footage still looks tall, the factor is too low.

COMMON MISTAKES

Common mistakes (and fast fixes).

Cropping instead of desqueezing

Crop hides the problem. Correct geometry first, then choose delivery framing.

Choosing the wrong factor

Preview faces and circles — if they look off, adjust factor before export.

Exporting before previewing

Always check framing + geometry in preview mode (Fit / True) first.

Forgetting final delivery ratio

Decide whether you’re delivering 16:9, 2.39:1, or social crops after correction.
